leverage.exposure: The balance is negative and has not moved since the previous run. That costs nothing until the instant the matchday locks, and the lock is more than four days away, so it does not block the buy — but it must be unwound before then, because a negative balance at matchday start scores zero for the entire matchday and that risk outranks everything else here. The unwind path is clean and has slack: the Hwang sale alone turns the balance positive, and the Pinckert buy then reopens a deficit that one further sale from the flagged three closes with room to spare. Sequence matters — buy first, sell second — because the sale is what the buy funds, not a precondition for it. Keep the flip legs sized against what is left after the buy, not against the headline spending power, and remember every flip must be unwound to a non-negative balance and at least eleven players before the lock.

binding_gap: Centre-back quality, not headcount. The squad is above the minimum and the shape is legal, so there is no penalty exposure on numbers. The gap is that one of the four defensive slots is filled by the cheapest body in the squad, on an average barely a quarter of what the slot is worth, while two of the other three are doubtful. That is the slot Pinckert fills, and filling it is worth more than any flip on the board.

verdict.headline: A quiet league and a loud squad.
verdict.headline_short: A quiet league and a loud squad.
verdict.detail: A quiet league and a loud squad. Nothing has happened on the board since the previous run — the newest listing predates that run's own stamp — but the eleven Georg would field on Friday now carries three men with dated, verified doubts, and the board holds exactly one body worth fixing that with. The run reverses the standing decision to leave Lukas Pinckert on the watch list and makes him a buy, which in turn caps the flip book: points outrank the tick, and the capital cannot serve both.

sell.reason: Hwang remains the standing sale and the call is unchanged, at a price the live squad read confirms to the cent. He is the twelfth man, he is unplaced, his average is the weakest in the squad, and selling him back to Kickbase pays exactly his market value with no spread. That single action clears the deficit outright and turns the balance positive — it is free in points and it is the thing that unlocks the rest of the cycle. The second sale is the one Georg should NOT make yet. Funding the buy back to a non-negative balance needs one more body, and the two candidates are not equivalent. Engelhardt is the better economic exit: he is injured with no return timeline, and his value is falling hard both on the day and within the hour, so every hour held costs money. Brackelmann is the safer structural exit: his value is rising, but selling him keeps the shape at four-four-two, which is confirmed legal, whereas selling Engelhardt leaves five defenders and three midfielders and needs a five-three-two that this run has NOT been able to verify as fillable. Do not execute either on this run. The lock is more than four days out, the lineups firm up Thursday, and the right move is to sell whichever of the flagged three is confirmed out — with the formation picker checked in the app first if Engelhardt is the one.

buy.reason: Pinckert is the buy, and this is a deliberate reversal of previous runs, which parked him as a watch and left the capital committed to the flip book instead. That ordering was wrong under a points mandate. He is a centre-back who has started every league game this season and played essentially every available minute, in a back three his coach has publicly backed; the only two fitness items against him are both older than his current run and both resolved, one an illness that cost him a single game and one a return to training, since when he has started throughout. He carries no Kickbase status flag and his value is rising. The points case needs no speculation about injuries at all: he walks into the back four ahead of Nakuzola, which is a straight upgrade on the fielded eleven before any sale, and it simultaneously converts Nakuzola from a starting liability into the bench cover the squad does not currently have for two doubtful centre-backs. The premium over his market value is modest and it is a manager ask, not a contested Kickbase listing, so the high cluster is the wrong yardstick — pay the ask rather than countering at market value. The listing is only hours old, so the rule about stale asks inviting a lowball does not yet apply, and every auction this ledger has lost was lost by underbidding. Crucially, the buy clears on spending power alone and needs no sale first: buy, then unwind. Banzuzi was the only other body tested against the midfield mandate and he fails on price — his ask sits around six times the measured manager band, and his average is below the man he would replace. He is logged as an avoid with a price-based reversal condition, and his club was corrected in the ledger along the way: he is a Leipzig player, not a Schalke one.
